The operational status shows all features are active and deployed as of 2026-04-08. Known issues/limitations include: MemPalace evaluation was deferred (re-evaluate around 2026-04-22) due to viral hype, retracted claims, and security issues (shell injection, unpinned ChromaDB, macOS segfault); the Aegis project is in Phase 1.A with no code yet; Trivy should not be used due to supply-chain compromise; zen/*-free models should not be registered in consumer configs; Max token has ~1h TTL and OpenAI token has ~7d TTL requiring periodic refresh; Kubo's OpenClaw OAuth token is separate from LiteLLM and requires separate refresh (not covered by /subscription-refresh skill); Kubo LiteLLM models are mirror-synced with skip prefixes to avoid billing conflicts.

Recent changes deployed on 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-02 include: env-masker deployment (secret masking for .env files across Claude Code sessions and LiteLLM); Erudito v3 agentic search (non-git knowledge base folders + LLM-powered decompose+retrieve+synthesize queries); session onboarding via SessionStart hook replacing manual checklist functions, with simplified aliases (cc/ccr/ccc/ccp/ccf); mesh operational improvements (config sync, daily health cron, hook validator, Kubo tmux bridge); security-guidance plugin patched to skip documentation files and avoid false positives; and Opencode Zen + Go keys split per node to track spending separately. Previous changes documented include: Erudito v3 reengineering (2026-03-18) with NotebookLM integration; policy-based node detection; and Kubo OpenClaw setup with OAuth Pro (2026-03-29).

This is a personal AI-Lab infrastructure project run by a single user (r0calex) across multiple machines (Hanzo as main, Sariatu as secondary, Kubo as satellite). It provides a self-hosted AI development environment with unified model access through LiteLLM, knowledge management through Erudito with NotebookLM validation, secret masking through env-masker, and supply-chain security through Aegis. The system is designed for mesh-wide access to premium models (Max Haiku, OpenAI Pro) without per-token costs through subscriptions. Quality standards are strict: once deployed, the quality level becomes the minimum and must never regress. All projects are documented with specs, plans, implementation reports (IRs), and standard operating procedures (SOPs), stored either in claude_contracts/ or within the project repos themselves (like Aegis docs inside ~/ai-lab/aegis/docs/).
